key_insight: BRACE jointly learns a Bayesian belief over user intent and an assistance policy end-to-end, so assistance adapts dynamically to uncertainty and context. This unified optimization yields higher task success while better preserving user agency than static blending or separate inference/arbitration pipelines.
problem_solved: Addresses the mismatch between separate goal inference and assistance arbitration in shared autonomy — eliminating reliance on fixed blending ratios and improving robustness in unstructured, uncertain environments while respecting user control.
method: Differentiable Bayesian belief module with context encoding to maintain and update probabilistic intent estimates from user inputs and observations.
Reinforcement learning of an assistance policy conditioned on the belief state, trained end-to-end so gradients flow through belief updates to align inference with downstream assistance objectives.
Objective balances task performance and a user-agency/comfort term, producing context-sensitive, uncertainty-aware assistance without hand-tuned blending rules.
impact: Provides a practical template for building adaptive, principled shared-autonomy systems that are both more effective and more respectful of user intent. Practitioners can replace brittle pipelines with a single end-to-end trainable model that generalizes better to real-world variability.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensors → Bayesian belief + context encoder → RL policy → robot action (with feedback loop from user), highlighting end-to-end gradient flow
Belief evolution graphic: sequence of probability distributions showing uncertainty reduction and how assistance changes under high vs low confidence
Performance chart: bar/line comparison vs baselines (static blending, separate inference) on task success and agency metrics
Trade-off curve: assistance strength vs user-agency metric illustrating how BRACE negotiates the balance
paper_title: End-to-end Optimization of Belief and Policy Learning in Shared Autonomy Paradigms
paper_authors: MH Farhadi, Ali Rabiee, Sima Ghafoori, Anna Cetera, Andrew Fisher
